entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, and the six Mores kept; no inputs and no done_at. The deliverable is for the developers of invoicer, who use it to know whom invoicer serves (the accounting team, who print invoices with the command, and the developers who call the library and install the command) and what each achieves, so that each change leans toward those ends.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with its template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
The job, from the goal: invoicer turns the invoice lines a team keeps into each client invoice with right totals.
Roles by their part of the job: the accounting team, who print each client invoice with the command; the developer, who calls invoicer as a library from their own code (Cut decision N1/0).
The accounting team prints only once someone installs the command; a developer installs it once, so installing belongs to the developer role (Cut decision N1/1).
No person left unclear: the Cut decisions settle both roles and the install, so nothing to ask.
No split: every member of the accounting team counts a right printed invoice as done; every developer counts their own code still working and the command installed.
No merge: the accounting team and the developers count different results as done.
Two roles, so neither is named user.

O1 the accounting team bills each client what that client owes, without asking a developer; O2 the developers own code keeps giving the results it gave before; O3 a developer installs the command once, and it runs for the accounting team from then on.
Why asked of each: billing what is owed, code that keeps working, and an install done once are ends in the roles own work, not things invoicer does.
Three distinct ends: a developer can keep their own code working without installing the command, and install it without the accounting team printing; so three objectives.

Tasks: O1 from starting a client invoice to holding it printed; O2 from updating invoicer to their own code running as before; O3 from starting the install to the command running for the accounting team.

How well, as failure shares: KR1.1 print tasks that end without the right invoice or with a developer help; KR2.1 library calls in their own code that give a different result after an update; KR3.1 installs that end without the command running for the accounting team.
How fast: KR1.2 time from starting a client invoice to holding it printed, fixing lines included; KR2.2 edits to their own code after an update, as effort; KR3.2 the developer time for the install.
Each of the six key results says Lower is better.
One order of all six, as the Cut decision N4/0 sets: KR2.1, KR1.1, KR3.1, KR1.2, KR2.2, KR3.2; a change is kept only if no key result ranked above the one it improves gets worse.
No targets; that and its reason, Goodhart law, are two sentences.

Work the Cut decisions name: print from invoice lines in the spreadsheet; the rate set at each print; one rounding; a failed print naming the line; the command only calling the library; the one install.
Invoice lines O1; rate at each print O1; one rounding O2 (O1 takes its totals from it, Cut decision N5/0); failed print naming the line O1; command only calling the library O2; the install O3.

Each pair has a piece that serves one alone: the failed print O1 not O2, the command only calling the library O2 not O1, the install O3 alone; no merge. O3 no longer counts the accounting team asking for help, which is O1 alone.
The rounding named O1 and O2; it names O2 alone, as the Cut decision N5/0 sets, and O1 takes its totals from it.
Every piece serves an objective; nothing to ask.
The person gave the one way and its ideas (Cut decisions N6/0 and N6/1); nothing more to ask.
The one way, as the person accepted it: invoicer turns invoice lines into an invoice whose totals are right without anyone redoing the math.

Five ideas, each with what it gives: invoice lines from the spreadsheet O1; rate at each print, not saved per client O1; one rounding O2; a print that goes wrong tells the accounting team what to fix O1; the command adds to invoicer without changing it O2.

Moments: the developer installs the command; the accounting team takes the invoice lines, sets the rate, prints, meets a print that goes wrong and prints again; a developer updates invoicer under their own code and calls the library.

Each moment has its idea: taking lines, invoice lines from the spreadsheet; the rate, set at each print; the totals and library calls, one rounding; a print that goes wrong, it names the line; an update, the command adds without changing. The install takes no idea, as the person said.
The two proposed ideas were put to the person in round 1, who said yes to both as worded (Cut decision N6/1); no new idea proposed.
All five ideas kept: each holds the one way at a moment no other covers, and the person decided both new ones join; this goes past the template three, which the Made names as settled.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end. Roles says who comes; Objectives and key results says what each achieves and how it is measured; Concept says the one way and its ideas.
Readers: the developers of invoicer, who weigh a change against whom invoicer serves and what each achieves.
The developers know invoicer and its library; they come to learn the roles, the objectives and their ranking, and the concept.
Three sections of one topic each; a developer reads each whole for its purpose, so no split.
Each role, objective, key result and idea is a list item with its own name, as the template sets; no new headings.
The ranking of the six key results is an order, so a numbered list; roles, objectives and ideas stay bulleted lists; the why of no targets stays prose.
Readers words from the goal and the person: invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, print, library, their own code, install, accounting team.
Chosen: invoice lines, their own code, the accounting team, the command, the library; no coined term to define.
Facts in more than one place: where the invoice lines come from (Roles, KR1.2, Concept); the rate at each print (Roles, Concept); the accounting team printing without a developer (O1, O3, KR3.1).
The Concept alone keeps the source of the invoice lines and the rate at each print (Cut decision N3/0); O1 alone keeps printing without a developer (Cut decision N5/0).
No two places state a fact differently; nothing to ask.
Grouped names: spreadsheet lines and invoice lines; own programs, own code and existing library calls; the team and the accounting team; a change to invoicer and an update of invoicer.
Kept: invoice lines, their own code, the accounting team (Cut decision N3/0); update of invoicer for what developers take, a change for what the developers of invoicer weigh.
No name refers to two things once update and change are kept apart.

Took each Cut decision as it stands; settled by the best practices the O3 and KR3.1 rewording to the one install, KR1.2 starting at the print task without naming the spreadsheet, the ranking as a numbered list, and keeping five concept ideas; no point left open.
